abstract: PURPOSE/OBJECTIVE: To investigate whether exogenous PUMA expression suppresses the growth of drug-resistant choriocarcinoma cells and sensitizes them to chemotherapeutic agents. METHODS: An adenovirus expressing PUMA (Ad-PUMA), alone or in combination with chemotherapeutic agents (5-FU, vp16, MTX), was used to treat drug-resistant choriocarcinoma cells jeg-3/vp16 and parental jeg-3. The growth inhibitory and proapoptotic effects of Ad-PUMA both in vitro and in vivo were examined. The mechanisms of PUMA-mediated growth suppression and apoptosis were investigated by an analysis of caspase 3 activation and the change of mitochondrial membrane potential. The levels of PUMA, p53 and caspase 3 were detected by Western blotting. RESULT: PUMA was expressed lower in jeg-3/vp16 than in jeg-3. jeg-3/vp16 responded much less sensitively to 5-FU and vp16 treatment than jeg-3, though PUMA was up-regulated in both cells. Exogenous PUMA expression resulted in potent growth suppression of jeg-3/vp16 and jeg-3 through induction of apoptosis. Ad-PUMA sensitized jeg-3 and jeg-3/vp16 to chemotherapeutic agents. When Ad-PUMA 10MOI and 5-FU, vp16 or MTX were combined respectively, IC50 of drugs decreased by 8.66-, 18.66- and 13.06-fold compared with those treated by anticancer drugs alone in jeg-3/vp16, while in jeg-3, IC50 decreased only by 1.80-, 1.78- and 2.76-fold. Ad-PUMA restored the sensitivity of choriocarcinoma cells to chemotherapeutic agents by enhancing apoptosis induced by anticancer drugs. Similar results could be observed in vivo. Xenograft tumors were inhibited by Ad-PUMA or vp16. In the drug-resistant group, the inhibitory rate increased from 14.57% to 78.93% in vp16 and vp16 combined with Ad-PUMA subgroups. While in the parental group, the inhibitory rate increased but slightly, from 66.39% to 71.56%. CONCLUSION: PUMA is an important player in the therapeutic responses to chemotherapeutic agents of choriocarcinoma cells. In addition to its role in inhibiting tumor growth, low dose of Ad-PUMA significantly restored the sensitivity of choriocarcinoma cells to chemotherapeutic agents in vitro and in vivo. Exogenous PUMA is potentially useful as a sensitizer in treating drug-resistant choriocarcinoma.
abstract_ja: 目的：薬剤耐性絨毛癌細胞の増殖を、外因性PUMA発現が抑制し、化学療法薬への感受性を高めるかを検討すること。方法：PUMAを発現するアデノウイルス(Ad-PUMA)を単独、または化学療法薬(5-FU、VP16、MTX)と併用し、薬剤耐性絨毛癌細胞JEG-3/VP16と親株JEG-3を処理した。Ad-PUMAのin vitroおよびin vivoにおける増殖抑制作用とアポトーシス誘導作用を検討した。PUMA、p53、カスパーゼ3の発現をウエスタンブロットで検出し、カスパーゼ3の活性化とミトコンドリア膜電位の変化を解析した。結果：JEG-3/VP16ではJEG-3に比べPUMAの発現が低かった。JEG-3/VP16はJEG-3に比べて5-FUおよびVP16に対する感受性が著しく低かったが、両細胞ともPUMAは上昇していた。外因性PUMA発現は、JEG-3/VP16とJEG-3の両方でアポトーシスを介した強い増殖抑制をもたらした。Ad-PUMAは、JEG-3およびJEG-3/VP16の化学療法薬感受性を高めた。Ad-PUMA 10MOIと5-FU、VP16、MTXをそれぞれ併用すると、JEG-3/VP16では薬剤単独に比べIC50が8.66倍、18.66倍、13.06倍低下したが、JEG-3ではそれぞれ1.80倍、1.78倍、2.76倍の低下にとどまった。Ad-PUMAは抗がん剤によって誘導されるアポトーシスを増強することで、絨毛癌細胞の化学療法感受性を回復させた。in vivoでも同様の結果が得られた。異種移植腫瘍において、Ad-PUMAまたはVP16によって腫瘍増殖が抑制された。薬剤耐性群では、VP16単独およびVP16とAd-PUMAの併用群で阻害率が14.57%から78.93%に上昇した。一方、親株群では阻害率は66.39%から71.56%へわずかに上昇したのみだった。結論：PUMAは絨毛癌細胞の化学療法への治療反応において重要な役割を果たす。腫瘍増殖抑制への寄与に加え、低用量のAd-PUMAは、in vitroおよびin vivoで絨毛癌細胞の感受性を有意に回復させた。外因性PUMAは、薬剤耐性絨毛癌の治療における感受性増強剤として有用となる可能性がある。
